title: Beehive Weight Nectar-Flow and Swarm Alert
dataSources: Beehive telemetry (`beehive:reading`), coop door (`chickencoop:door`), egg counts (`egg:count`), livestock tags (`livestock:tag`), feed level (`feed:level`), pasture sensors (`pasture:sensor`).
app: Homestead sensors — connected beehive scale/temperature/sound, automatic chicken-coop door, egg counter, livestock GPS/health tags, feed-silo level, and pasture soil sensors — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and LoRaWAN gateways.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=beehive:reading
| timechart span=1h avg(weight_kg) as weight
| streamstats current=f last(weight) as prev
| eval change=weight-prev, sudden_drop=if(change<-1.5,1,0)
description: Watches hive weight to see nectar coming in day by day and flags a sudden drop that can signal a swarm leaving.
value: Hive weight is the beekeeper's vital sign; it reveals nectar flow, stores for winter, and the abrupt loss that means a swarm.
implementation: Feed a hive scale into `index=personal`; review the weight trend and alert on a sudden large drop.
visualization: Time chart of hive weight with sudden-drop markers.
grandmaExplanation: It watches how heavy the beehive is to see honey building up and warns if the bees suddenly swarm away.
